overview: EVT Limited (formerly Event Hospitality and Entertainment) is an Australian diversified leisure and hospitality group operating cinema exhibition under the Event Cinemas and Birch Carroll & Coyle brands in Australia and New Zealand and CineStar in Germany, hotels and resorts under Rydges, QT, Atura, LyLo and the Independent Collection (plus the third-party management platform Connect Hospitality), the Thredbo Alpine Resort in the NSW Snowy Mountains, and a portfolio of commercial property. The Group's stated strategy (branded 'EVT' for Entertainment, Ventures and Travel) is to grow revenue above market, maximise the value of its hotel property portfolio via asset-light expansion and capital recycling, and pursue business transformation to protect margins, with Hotels now explicitly positioned as the Group's primary future growth platform.

business_model.summary: EVT earns box-office, food & beverage and screen-advertising revenue from a large but shrinking cinema circuit (the 'Fewer, Better' strategy), room, food & beverage and conferencing revenue from owned hotels, growing fee-based management income from branded (EVT Hotels & Resorts) and third-party (Connect Hospitality) management agreements, seasonal lift-ticket, accommodation and activity revenue from Thredbo, and episodic gains from property development/divestment. Cinema and Thredbo revenue is largely transactional/seasonal and highly dependent on film slate and weather; hotel management fees are more recurring; owned hotel and cinema earnings are asset-heavy and operationally leveraged.

revenue_streams.name: Hotels and Resorts (EVT Hotels & Resorts + Connect Hospitality)
Entertainment Australia & New Zealand (Event Cinemas, BCC)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (moviegoers, hotel guests, ski/resort visitors) with a growing B2B component (third-party hotel owners paying management/franchise fees under Connect Hospitality, and corporate/conference customers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily Australia and New Zealand (cinemas, hotels, Thredbo), with a material German cinema circuit (CineStar) and expanding hotel footprint into Southeast Asia (Singapore, Thailand) and the Pacific (Fiji)

main_competitors: IHG, Marriott, TFE Hotels, Crown Resorts, independent operators (hotels)
Streaming services (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon) as substitutes for cinema
Other Australian alpine resorts (Perisher, Falls Creek, Mt Buller) for Thredbo
competitive_position.market_position: Historically Australia's largest cinema exhibitor (Event Cinemas), though HOYTS has reported market share gains and now claims the number-one Australian position by some measures; EVT remains the larger operator in New Zealand. In hotels, EVT states it is the second-largest hotel operator in Australia/New Zealand by room count behind Accor, with Rydges, QT, Atura and LyLo spanning midscale to upscale/lifestyle segments.

moat_factors.description: Large, often freehold cinema and hotel sites in prime CBD and tourist locations (e.g., State Theatre, QT Sydney, Thredbo's exclusive resort lease) are difficult for competitors to replicate
Multiple distinct hotel brands (QT lifestyle, Rydges upscale, Atura/LyLo budget-lifestyle) and Event Cinemas/Cinebuzz loyalty programme provide some customer stickiness and segment coverage
IMAX, ScreenX, Gold Class, Vmax and DX formats support pricing power and differentiate against value-focused competitors, though HOYTS is expanding its own IMAX footprint
Long-dated lease over the Thredbo Alpine Resort gives EVT a geographically protected, high-barrier-to-entry asset within the NSW ski market

moat_factors.factor: Diversification across cinema, hotels, alpine and property
moat_factors.description: Reduces reliance on any single earnings stream, though management itself is now trying to reduce the volatility of cinema/weather-exposed earnings by re-weighting toward hotels

weaknesses: Cinema admissions remain structurally below pre-COVID levels in most markets despite the 'Fewer, Better' strategy
Reliance on third-party Hollywood/local film studios for content supply, with limited ability to influence release windows or slates
Owned-hotel and cinema earnings are asset-heavy, capital intensive and exposed to weather, construction disruption and macro/consumer-confidence swings

Complex multi-segment conglomerate structure (cinemas, hotels, alpine, property) that the Group itself is now reviewing with Rothschild & Co, suggesting the market may be under-valuing the parts versus a simplified structure
Smaller scale than global hotel groups (Accor, IHG, Marriott) in brand distribution, loyalty network size and access to capital for international expansion

growth_drivers: Pivot to Hotels as 'primary future growth platform': asset-light expansion via EVT Hotels & Resorts (Independent Collection, new builds, acquisitions such as QT Auckland) and the third-party Connect Hospitality management platform (seeded by the Pro-invest Hotels acquisition, now managing a growing portfolio of franchised hotels)

Completion of major capex-heavy redevelopments (QT Queenstown seismic/room upgrade, LyLo Gold Coast) expected to convert into incremental EBITDA and stronger cash conversion from FY2027 as projects roll off

~$800 million non-core property divestment programme over three years (including the George and Market Street, Sydney precinct and 70 George Street) recycling capital into higher-returning hotel growth and potentially funding special dividends

Continued 'Fewer, Better' cinema strategy — exiting marginal sites and investing in premium formats (IMAX, ScreenX, DX, Gold Class, Vmax) — management estimates a further ~$ (unspecified) million of incremental annual EBITDA as more sites are exited
Expansion of hotel brands into new geographies (Singapore, Thailand, Fiji) and new lifestyle/budget sub-brands (LyLo, Atura Snuggy) broadening the addressable market

Investment in AI-driven customer engagement, search/Generative Engine Optimisation and agentic commerce (e.g., Mastercard agentic payments pilot) aimed at protecting direct booking channels and reducing distribution costs

Independent Board-led Group structure review (advised by Rothschild & Co) that could unlock value via a simplification, demerger or other restructuring of the conglomerate, though no outcome or timeline has been confirmed as of the FY2026 AGM (October 2026)

business.description: Entertainment division relies on a high-quality global film release schedule; strikes, studio strategy changes, shortened theatrical windows or weak slates directly hit admissions and revenue, and EVT has little ability to mitigate this

Highly competitive cinema (HOYTS, Village) and hotel (Accor, IHG, Marriott, independents) markets; shifting customer discovery via AI-driven search/agentic commerce could reduce direct channel visibility and market share
Major projects (QT Queenstown, QT Gold Coast, LyLo Gold Coast, Event Bondi redevelopment) create temporary earnings drag and execution risk during build-out
Hospitality-sector wage inflation, staff shortages, and heightened scrutiny of underpayment and psychosocial/workplace-culture issues across the industry

financial.description: ~$3+ billion property portfolio (owned hotels, Thredbo, cinema real estate) is subject to periodic independent revaluation; declines (as seen at Thredbo in FY2026) can affect balance sheet strength and market perception
Net debt rose at 31 December 2025 versus 30 June 2025 following the ~A$[redacted]-million Pro-invest Hotels management acquisition; further bolt-on M&A or buybacks could add leverage
Group had no interest rate hedges in place as at 30 June 2026 per the FY2026 annual report, leaving floating-rate bank debt exposed to rate movements
NZD- and EUR-denominated earnings (New Zealand cinemas/hotels, CineStar Germany) create translation exposure to AUD

regulatory.description: Operations across Australia, New Zealand, Germany and emerging Asia-Pacific markets expose the Group to differing labour, consumer, licensing, and hotel-franchise regulatory regimes
FY2026 was the first year EVT reported under AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures, adding compliance burden and disclosure risk around physical/transition climate risks (notably for Thredbo)
Standard listed-company risk of regulatory action, reputational damage or class actions for disclosure breaches

macro.description: Cinema, hotel leisure/conferencing and Thredbo visitation are discretionary and sensitive to consumer confidence; management explicitly flagged softer corporate conference/events demand in Q4 FY2026 tied to broader macro uncertainty and the Middle East conflict
Thredbo's EBITDA is highly dependent on snowfall/weather (poor June openings recur) and summer bushfire activity also curtailed FY2026/FY2027 visitation; hotel RevPAR is similarly seasonal
Group explicitly cites pandemic, geopolitical conflict and energy price shocks as capable of materially affecting operations, given reliance on travel and discretionary leisure spend

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian/NZ cinema admissions continue to recover gradually from COVID-19 and the Hollywood strikes but remain below pre-pandemic levels, with growth increasingly reliant on blockbuster slates and premium-format monetisation rather than volume; the Australian hotel market is supported by resilient inbound/domestic tourism and RevPAR growth, with branded/asset-light management agreements an industry-wide growth avenue (mirroring global hotel groups' shift to fee-based models)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — cinema and hotel conferencing/leisure spend are discretionary and track consumer confidence; Thredbo is additionally weather-cyclical; property/divestment gains are episodic
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — floating-rate bank debt (increased secured facility to fund Pro-invest and growth capex) with no interest rate hedges in place as at 30 June 2026
key_input_costs: Labour and wages (hospitality and cinema staff)
Construction/refurbishment costs for hotel and cinema redevelopments

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results (year ended 30 June 2026): normalised revenue $1,314.9m (+6.3%), normalised EBITDA $174.4m (+8.4%), normalised profit after tax ~$54.3m (+41.3%), reported NPAT $50.7m (+51.9%); final fully franked dividend of 23 cents per share declared
Management announced an ~$800 million non-core property divestment programme over three years, to be recycled into hotel growth, with the Board to consider special dividends from proceeds
Independent Board Committee continuing the Group structure review with Rothschild & Co as adviser; no outcome announced, flagged as a key FY2027 strategic priority

H1 FY2026 result (half year to 31 Dec 2025): normalised revenue $683.8m (+5.4%), normalised EBITDA $105.1m (+5.5%), reported NPAT $37.8m (+21.6%); interim dividend raised to 18.0 cents (fully franked) from 16.0 cents

Completed acquisition of the Pro-invest Hotels management business, establishing the Connect Hospitality third-party hotel management platform; annualised earnings tracking at the upper end of the ~guidance range provided at acquisition
Completed acquisition of QT Auckland, expanding the QT brand into New Zealand's largest market
Sale of Rydges Geelong completed (retained under a long-term brand licence), consistent with the capital recycling/asset-light strategy
AGM held; no confirmed update on the Group structure review outcome reported publicly as of mid-November 2026
QT Queenstown and QT Gold Coast redevelopment/seismic works caused temporary earnings disruption through FY2026, with benefits expected to flow through progressively from FY2027
Thredbo FY2027 summer trading affected by bushfire-related visitation disruption; full-year EBITDA guided to around previously flagged levels, subject to June 2027 winter weather

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jane Hastings has repositioned Hotels as EVT's 'primary future growth platform', citing the completion of Connect Hospitality and the 'three-pillar' hotel framework (owned EVT Hotels & Resorts, asset-light/Independent Collection, and third-party Connect Hospitality management) as unlocking growth across all hotel market segments. Management reiterated that while major hotel redevelopment capex (QT Queenstown, LyLo Gold Coast) is near completion, this should lead to materially stronger earnings conversion and cash generation from FY2027. The Board has launched a Group structure review (with Rothschild & Co as independent adviser) to assess options to maximise hotel value and shareholder returns, with no certainty of any resulting transaction and updates to come as outcomes are reached, balanced against confidentiality.

bull_case: Clear strategic pivot toward a higher-quality, more capital-light, fee-based Hotels earnings mix (Connect Hospitality, Independent Collection) should improve the Group's earnings quality and valuation multiple over time

Major capex-heavy hotel redevelopments (QT Queenstown, LyLo Gold Coast) are nearing completion, setting up a step-change in earnings conversion and free cash flow from FY2027 without a corresponding step-up in capex

~$800 million non-core property divestment programme could unlock trapped capital, fund special dividends/buybacks, and re-rate the stock if divestments are achieved near or above book/independent valuations
Independent Group structure review (Rothschild & Co) creates an identifiable, market-recognised catalyst for a potential simplification or demerger that could close any sum-of-the-parts discount

Entertainment division delivering strong operating leverage from the 'Fewer, Better' strategy — EBITDA growth materially outpacing admissions growth — demonstrates resilient underlying cinema economics even with a smaller circuit
Record Hotels results and continued RevPAR growth across key Australian and NZ markets (Sydney, Perth, Adelaide, Queenstown, Christchurch) show durable demand for EVT's hotel brands
bear_case: Group structure review has been running for an extended period with no confirmed outcome as of the October 2026 AGM, creating overhang/uncertainty risk that a transaction may not materialise or may disappoint

Cinema admissions remain structurally below pre-COVID levels and the business remains fully exposed to unpredictable global film release slates and studio strategy shifts (e.g., shortened theatrical windows) outside EVT's control

Discretionary, weather- and macro-sensitive revenue base (hotel conferencing, Thredbo snow seasons, cinema box office) leaves earnings vulnerable to any consumer-confidence downturn, as already evidenced by softer Q4 FY2026 corporate/conference demand and bushfire-hit Thredbo summer trading

Execution risk around multiple concurrent large redevelopments (QT Queenstown, QT Gold Coast, LyLo Gold Coast, Event Bondi) has already caused repeated guidance trims and could continue to disrupt near-term earnings

Competitive intensity is rising on both fronts — HOYTS gaining Australian cinema market share and expanding its own IMAX footprint, and large global hotel groups (Accor, IHG, Marriott) dominating branded room share — constraining EVT's ability to grow share organically
No interest rate hedges in place as at 30 June 2026 leaves the Group's debt-funded growth (Pro-invest, QT Auckland, redevelopment capex) exposed to rising funding costs
